properties.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lot 4111009 (recorded 2019-02-07; mapped 2019-03-14; active); cross-checked against Pier 70 Design for Development Figure 6.4.2 - Building Height Maximum (p.155).
properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. RE-TRACED 2026-09-16 (full Pier 70 geometry restart, after a systematic pass found 9 of this site's other 'trusted' parcels were meaningfully wrong): re-measured programmatically instead of by eye, for consistency with the rest of this site -- isolated this legend color (RGB [128,193,219]) and extracted a clean rectangular contour (OpenCV) at pixel (1203,437)-(1401,682). Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. Result is close to (within ~5m of) the prior hand-read version -- this parcel's own corners were already read correctly; kept for methodological consistency across the site. Still overlaps 'Noonan Building' by ~2843 m2 -- an already-documented, expected overlap given Noonan's own low-confidence, directional-only placement. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the 'Building 14 footprint' identified by blklot 4052001 refers to a legacy lot id: DataSF Building Footprints carry mblr SF4052001 on 21 footprints in the repo copy (data/raw/buildings.geojson), the data do not show which is Building 14, and blklot 4052001 was retired on 2018-10-02 (DataSF Assessor parcels, acdm-wktn), so it is not a current Assessor lot. No outside source is cited for that identification. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built (Port Item 11A, Aug 2026: the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'), and no source read ties it to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor parcels include new lots created for the 28-acre district in 2019, without street addresses, but which lot (if any) is Parcel A's was not established. It currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. EXTENDED SOUTH 2026-09-17 (user-flagged): this block's south edge fell ~11m short of the real sidewalk visible in satellite imagery, leaving a strip of unclaimed vacant land between the block and the street -- consistent with this site's known local scale error for parcels far from the transform's Illinois/Michigan St anchors (see Parcel E1's digitization_method for the same root cause). The diagram itself (Figure 6.4.2) shows this block's fill running right up to the street with no setback, so extended the two south vertices by 11m (measured via satellite pixel-color transition to the real sidewalk, 3 sample transects) to close the gap, matching the diagram's own convention rather than re-deriving the whole transform.'; notes: 'Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat.'. REPLACED 2026-10-10 (shape; status and use unchanged): the owner asked for the planned blocks that have Assessor lots under them to use those lots. DataSF's Assessor layer (data/raw/parcels.geojson) has Assessor lot 4111009 (5,013 m2, active, recorded 2019-02-07), 76% of our earlier trace lies inside it and the trace covers 81% of it; against the satellite imagery the lot lines sit on the real block edges where the trace was a few metres off. The outline is now that lot using the lots' own vertices (no simplification), in place of the traced shape of 5,307 m2. This identification is an inference from location, shape and size; no Port document read names the lot. geometry_type is now 'real' because the edges are recorded lot lines. The earlier sign-off covered the traced shape; this replacement was made at the owner's direction. 2026-10-12 CORRECTION to the 2026-10-10 entry above (text only; the shape is unchanged): its sentence 'against the satellite imagery the lot lines sit on the real block edges where the trace was a few metres off' was repeated across several Pier 70 shapes and no satellite comparison of this shape's edges is recorded, so the sentence is withdrawn for it. The lot is 5,013 m2 against a trace of 5,307 m2; 76% of the trace lies inside the lot and the trace covers 81% of it. No change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type.
properties.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 4111009, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. That this is the lot of Parcel A is Pier & Point's own inference from location, shape and size (our earlier trace of the D4D figure measured 5,307 m2 against the lot's 5,013 m2; 76% of the trace lies inside the lot and the trace covers 81% of it). No Port document read ties the lot number to it. A building may sit back from the lot lines. This block is not yet built (Port Item 11A, Aug 2026: the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'). It currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: No single Assessor lot is documented as Parcel A. Lot 4111009 (active) matches its location, shape and size, so its outline is Assessor lot 4111009; the identification is Pier & Point's inference, as the accuracy note says.
properties.regulatory_context: Commercial/life-science, 90 ft max / 6 stories per Figure 6.4.2. A revised design by Grimshaw with DES Architects + Engineers (356,400 sq ft, six stories, 90 ft) was reported by SF YIMBY in Oct 2021 with the refiled Development Agreement; King Street Properties announced in Feb 2023 a six-story, roughly 300,000 sq ft speculative life-science building on Parcel A (Bisnow). No source read links the Grimshaw design to King Street's plan, and no source read supports the earlier mention of a 2019 mass-timber design or a 365,000 GSF figure (removed 2026-09-29). No construction-start source found.
properties.notes: Parcel A of the Pier 70 Design for Development, shown as Assessor lot 4111009 (see the accuracy note).
